extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, publishers, research-integrity professionals, and academic researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Pre-publication screening and integrity checks to detect paper-mill / fraudulent manuscripts and to improve the quality of peer review, including automated flagging and manual verification procedures. Includes both AI/tool-based detection signals and publisher operational checklist items used before peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Similarity to known paper mill papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Looking for similarities with known paper mill papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of Wiley's Papermill Detection service (one of six tools) — automated comparison of incoming manuscripts against a corpus of known paper mill outputs to flag likely matches for editorial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search for 'tortured phrases' and problematic passages
rubrics_metrics.description: Searching for 'tortured phrases' and other problematic passages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect textual anomalies and unnatural paraphrases (a hallmark of paper-mill or automated text) as an automated signal to flag manuscripts for further human inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag irregular publishing patterns by authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Flagging 'irregular publishing patterns by paper authors'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect unusual author-level submission/publication behavior (e.g., many papers with similar structure/metadata) as an indicator of potential paper-mill activity; present such flags to editors for consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researcher identity verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Verifying researcher identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm authorship and institutional affiliation (not rely solely on provided contact info). Wiley and Hindawi practices include steps to verify authors; examples include matching authors' emails to prior publications and requiring authors to confirm via institutional addresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detect hallmarks of generative AI
rubrics_metrics.description: Detecting hallmarks of generative AI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automated detection of AI-generated text/images to flag manuscripts; signals are used to prompt human integrity checks rather than automatic rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze manuscript relevance to the journal
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyzing the relevance of a given manuscript to the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess topical fit and relevance algorithmically to catch submissions that seem mismatched or template-driven; used as one of multiple screening signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flagged papers routed to editor, not auto-rejected
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers will not automatically be rejected if they are flagged in the system – rather, they will be flagged to an editor for closer consideration before proceeding in the publishing workflow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guiding principle: AI/tool flags should supplement human integrity checks; final decisions rest with editors who perform further assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use AI tools to supplement human integrity checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Wiley’s Papermill Detection service is meant to supplement human integrity checks with AI-powered tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat automated signals as decisive; integrate them into an editorial workflow that includes human review and verification to avoid false positives and unjust rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage stakeholders to reduce incentives for paper mills
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct engagement with funders, universities and hospitals to create new incentives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy-level remedy: publishers should work with funders and institutions (per COPE/STM recommendations and initiatives like United2Act) to change reward structures that drive authors toward paper mills, rather than relying solely on detection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title uniqueness / not similar to previous studies
rubrics_metrics.description: The title should not be similar to previous studies. Otherwise, they ask the authors to change it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational check used by Hindawi ethics staff to detect recycled/template submissions; similarity of title to prior work is a trigger for asking the authors to revise the title or for rejection if suspicious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check for previous submission/rejection to same publisher
rubrics_metrics.description: They check to see if the paper or any version of it has been previously submitted to another Hindawi journal and rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a manuscript has prior rejections within the publisher network, that history must be reviewed as part of the screening process to understand prior concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial revision required after prior rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If the article is previously rejected by another Hindawi journal, the extent of changes should be considerable. Otherwise, reject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevent recycling of rejected manuscripts with minimal edits; require demonstrable, substantial revision or reject to avoid repeated low-quality resubmissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require rebuttal letter for previously rejected submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the article is previously rejected by another Hindawi journal, the authors must revise it properly and also send a Rebuttal Letter along with the submission, addressing the reviewers’ concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demand explicit documentation of how prior reviewer concerns were addressed to assess the sincerity and thoroughness of revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor and question unusually large author lists
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of authors. If there are too many authors (8 or more authors), they will suspect some papermill activity, and will ask the authors to explain explicitly why so many authors?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use author-count heuristics as a signal: require justification for large author lists and reject when explanations are insufficient, because inflated author lists can be a red flag for paper mills or guest authorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check author contribution and ethical declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: They read carefully the author contribution and ethical declarations reported in the manuscript, and in the case of smallest missings, they ask the authors to fix them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require complete, accurate contribution statements and ethics declarations; minor omissions should be corrected before the manuscript advances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require authors confirm finality of author list and order
rubrics_metrics.description: They ask the authors to confirm that the order and list of authors is final and no author will be added or removed in the middle of submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevent post-submission manipulation of authorship by requiring explicit confirmation that the author list is final at submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check all references individually
rubrics_metrics.description: They will check ALL the references, ONE by ONE. Meticulously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manual or assisted verification of references to ensure citations are real, relevant, and not artifacts of citation-stuffing or paper-mill templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid bulk citation; require relevance/explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are more than 3 references cited at once somewhere in the text, they ask the authors to avoid BULK CITATION and reduce the number of references, or explain each reference separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discourage indiscriminate grouped citations that obscure whether each cited work is truly relevant; require per-citation relevance explanations when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify reference relevance to citing sentence
rubrics_metrics.description: They check the relevance of EACH reference to the sentence that cites it. Once they asked me 'what is the relevance of reference X to the sentence citing it?' and I had to explain it to them!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors/staff should ensure each citation actually supports the claim it is attached to, to catch fabricated or irrelevant citations commonly used in paper-mill outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text-similarity screening (iThenticate)
rubrics_metrics.description: They check text similarity using iThenticate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use plagiarism/text-similarity tools as a routine screen; high similarity scores trigger further manual investigation rather than automatic acceptance/rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual author identity checks via previous publications
rubrics_metrics.description: They check EACH of the authors very carefully. They search the internet for EACH of the authors one by one and find their email addresses on their previous articles published before. They try their best to verify each author, without first trusting the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-check authors against external records (prior papers, institutional pages) to confirm identity and contact details; do not rely solely on information supplied in the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require each author to confirm authorship from their email
rubrics_metrics.description: They ask each author to reply from his email that he/she is really an author. Unless all authors don’t verify this, Hindawi will not move to the next step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandate explicit, verifiable confirmation of authorship from each listed author using their institutional/verified email addresses prior to progressing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require institutional verification when personal emails used
rubrics_metrics.description: Sometimes, they don’t believe the authors. For example, a couple of times, our first author was a medical resident with a personal email address. They DIDN'T believe us. They asked us to do one of the following: Either 1. The resident had to provide an academic email address. OR 2. The department head must send a signed letter on an official university sheet, verifying that this person is indeed a resident at her department. And the department head must do this from her Academic email address. OR 3. The same be done by the dean of the university, again on an official university sheet and using the academic email address of the dean. ALL OF THIS JUST TO VERIFY ONE AUTHOR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When author contact details are non-institutional, require stronger proof of affiliation (institutional email or official signed verification) to guard against fabricated authorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check integrity of editor and reviewers and conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: They meticulously check the integrity of the editor and reviewers, as well as any conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that editors and reviewers are legitimate and free from conflicts to prevent manipulation of peer review (e.g., fake editors/reviewers or coerced reviews).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor review thoroughness and invite more reviewers if too short
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel check the extent of reviews and if they are too short, they ask the editor to invite more reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational quality control: enforce minimum substance in peer reviews by measuring review length/depth and requiring additional reviewers when reviews are superficial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be prepared for trade-off: thorough security measures slow workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: These SECURITY measures are beyond awesome. But they have made the process very very very slow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledges operational cost: rigorous, multi-step screening and verification improve integrity but substantially increase time-to-decision; publishers must balance speed vs. integrity.
